findings: `meaning_history.senses[0].period` and `.certainty`: the wind sense is supported as attested in late Shang use, but the entry character 风 is the simplified form. Label the attested graph/record as 風 (or the early bird-shaped graph used for the wind word) rather than implying the modern simplified form itself was written then. The `has_sense` edge inherits this claim and should be corrected with it.

`summary` and `formation`: “the words sounded alike” risks stating the proposed whole-graph loan’s sound match as established. The dossier says the bird’s spoken name is uncertain; qualify the sound resemblance as the proposed mechanism, and keep it distinct from 凡’s later phonetic role.

`learner.overview`: “the words may have sounded alike” leaves the borrowing mechanism unclear. State that the bird-shaped sign may have been reused for “wind” because the old bird-name and “wind” may have sounded alike; preserve that the bird-name is uncertain.
